featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is Go to place whenever i am in South Bombay, Mazgaon Queen Mary Restaurant is a must-visit for breakfast. This is my go-to spot every single time I’m in the area—it’s almost a ritual now.

Their beja curry and keema are absolutely top-notch, full of rich, authentic flavors that hit the spot every time. Pair that with their classic Irani chai and soft, buttery bun maska, and you’ve got a perfect Bombay breakfast.

There’s something about the old-school charm and consistency here that keeps me coming back. Simple food, done right, with unbeatable taste.

Highly recommended if you want a true South Bombay breakfast experience!

featured_reviews.name: Rutesh Ajgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this restaurant and had a great experience. The vintage sitting space creates a wonderful atmosphere that complements the good food and quick service perfectly.

For the meal, I started with the Chicken Leg (4/5), which was a delicious Tandoori starter and very well cooked.

The Mutton Brain Masala (4/5) was another highlight, as the brain was perfectly prepared in a flavorful masala.

I also tried the Mutton Lazeez (4/5), a unique boneless gravy with a nice balance of sweet and spicy notes.

While the Tandoori Roti (3/5) was okay,

the Pudina Lemon (4/5) was a very refreshing drink to end the meal. Highly recommended for a solid meal in a cool setting!

featured_reviews.review_text: The food is good, specially the kheema and Omelette. We once tried Paya soup but it was very oily. For kheema, it's highly recommended..

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are looking for the best breakfast in Mazgaon, Queen Mary is a must visit. This place is known for its bun maska, cutting chai, fluffy omelettes and flavourful mutton kheema. It has that old school Mumbai cafe vibe where food is served fresh and without any unnecessary fuss. Perfect spot for an early morning breakfast in South Mumbai.

Sunday mornings at Queen Mary are especially lively, with the place almost full of regulars and families enjoying breakfast together. If you love exploring authentic breakfast places in Mumbai and want to experience a local favourite in Mazgaon, Queen Mary is worth adding to your list.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for seafood and had a great experience. Ordered 2 Bombil fry, crab lollipop, and a prawns & crab thali. The seafood was fresh and well-cooked, with balanced spices that didn’t overpower the natural flavours.

The Bombil fry was crispy on the outside and soft inside, the crab lollipop was tasty and nicely seasoned, and the prawns & crab thali was generous in quantity and very satisfying. Portions are good, and the pricing is quite affordable for the quality and freshness offered.

Overall, a reliable place for tasty, budget-friendly seafood. Would definitely recommend it to seafood lovers and would visit again.

featured_reviews.name: tushar alphonso
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Hidden Gem for Seafood Lovers!
Stepping into Restaurant was like discovering a true culinary treasure. This charming, intimate seafood restaurant, though small in size, delivers an experience from the moment you walk in, the ambiance wraps around you like a warm, welcoming net. It's cozy and tastefully decorated, creating the perfect setting for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. You can tell a lot of thought went into making the space feel both elegant and comfortable.

But let's talk about the star of the show: the seafood! Every dish we ordered was simply divine. The prawns koliwada, bombil fry, chicken lollipop, Surmai fry, PRAWNS biryani & Paneer Biryani, Potato Kappa was cooked to perfection, showcasing the incredible freshness of the ingredients. It's clear they pride themselves on sourcing good quality seafood. The flavors were vibrant, perfectly balanced, and truly unforgettable.

The service was also impeccable – attentive without being intrusive, and genuinely friendly.

If you're a seafood enthusiast looking for an extraordinary dining experience in a delightful setting, [Masta Gajali] is an absolute must-visit. It's a small place with a huge heart and even bigger flavors. Highly, highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Sangeeta J
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had ordered their Bombil Thali and Prawn Samosa through Zomato from their Mazgaon branch. I was highly impressed with the packing and the good portions of the Bombil pieces. The thali was not spicy or overloaded with masala, and the thali set menu was unique from the rest of the malvani restaurants that also sell Bombil thali. The gravies were really tasty and went well with the rice. The chapatis are huge and sufficient to fill your stomach easily.
Eating in a restaurant and getting home delivery changes the entire food experience, but I loved how they took special care for their home delivery order packing it well so that there is no spillage. Prawn Samosa is a unique dish and makes for a nice evening snack. The filling is decent.
Please keep up the good service and quality.
Abhinandan to the management and cooking team ❤️
